summary:
Lowfire is an advanced geospatial platform designed to monitor and analyze wildfire dynamics in Peru using satellite telemetry from NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS).

The platform features an intuitive and friendly 3D interactive map, tailored for Protected Area Managers, Environmental Planners, local authorities, and rural communities. Users can seamlessly navigate across national, regional, and local levels, zooming in dynamically to inspect thermal clusters, sensor distributions, and high-resolution coordinates through a dynamic information panel.

Furthermore, Lowfire integrates a smart token-filtered AI Diagnostic Engine, delivering automated tactical insights and risk assessments for each specific region. Backed by a high-speed DuckDB spatial pipeline and OLS sensor harmonization, Lowfire  transforms complex satellite data into actionable intelligence for rapid emergency response and environmental conservation.
details:
LowFire: Interactive 3D Satellite Fire Monitoring & AI Diagnostic Platform

LowFire is an intuitive geospatial web platform designed to help Protected Area Managers, Environmental Planners, local authorities, and rural communities monitor forest fires and compare recent thermal activity against historical baselines in Peru.

How It Works

  • Automated Ingestion & Harmonization: Every 10 minutes, our backend ingests near-real-time (NRT) and historical hotspot data from NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS). Records are deduplicated, mapped onto a 1 × 1 km grid, and standardized using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression to reconcile cross-sensor sensitivity differences onto a single unified scale.
  • Interactive 3D Map & Dynamic Panel: Users can smoothly navigate from a national overview down to departments, provinces, districts, or specific coordinates. Clicking any region updates a synchronized 3D WebGL map, an interactive temporal calendar, and a dynamic information panel displaying radiative power (FRP), local timestamps, and sensor breakdowns.
  • Token-Filtered AI Diagnostics: An integrated LLM engine (OpenCode) automatically generates concise, tactical risk assessments and field recommendations for each region. To optimize compute resources, a smart threshold filter triggers deep AI synthesis only when ignition risk or active hotspots exceed critical levels, falling back to preloaded environmental baselines during calm periods.

Benefits & Intended Impact

LowFire bridges the gap between raw satellite telemetry and local decision-making. By making complex orbital data accessible through a user-friendly 3D interface and clear AI summaries, response teams can rapidly identify unusual fire patterns, prioritize field patrols, and allocate preventive resources effectively.

Tools, Languages & Architecture

  • Data & Geospatial Processing: Python, DuckDB (sub-100ms spatial queries), Shapely, Apache Parquet, and GeoJSON.
  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js (WebGL).
  • AI & Infrastructure: OpenCode CLI (LLM synthesis), FastAPI, Nginx, and systemd on a Linux VPS.

Creativity & Key Considerations

Beyond standard 2D hotspot viewers, LowFire synchronizes 3D spatial clustering with historical seasonality and automated AI interpretation. Our team carefully accounted for orbital overpass differences, sensor resolution disparities (375m VIIRS vs. 1km MODIS), rendering performance for large datasets, and clear labeling so users always distinguish between raw satellite observations, harmonized metrics, and AI-generated insights.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
